name: Permanent Residence Permit (P Permit)

qualifying_event.description: Effective 8 January 2026, Finland replaced the previous flat 4-years-of-A-permit rule with 5 alternative qualification paths, each requiring a continuous (A) permit or Brexit permit as the base status.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Residence permit history, work/income/education records matching one of the 5 paths.

requirement_groups.name: Path 1: 6 years' residence + work history + B1 language

requirements.blocker_text: 6 years of residence under a continuous (A) permit or Brexit permit, with at least 2 years of work history in Finland and B1-level (satisfactory) Finnish or Swedish language skills.
4 years of residence under a continuous (A) permit or Brexit permit, with income subject to income tax of at least EUR 40,000 in the most recently completed tax assessment.

requirement_groups.name: Path 3: higher education degree completed in Finland

requirements.blocker_text: A higher-education degree completed in Finland qualifies under a separate path; exact residence/work-history minimums for this specific path were not confirmed at tier-1 precision in this pass.

requirement_groups.name: Path 4: degree completed outside Finland + work history

requirements.blocker_text: 4 years of residence, a recognised master's or doctoral degree completed outside Finland, and 2 years of work history in Finland.
4 years of residence, 3 years of work history in Finland, and C1-level Finnish or Swedish language proficiency.

evidence_required.document: Work history records / tax assessment / degree certificate / language test certificate (matching chosen path)

sources.title: Maahanmuuttovirasto -- Amendments to Aliens Act Regarding Permanent Residence Permits 2026: 5 alternative paths effective 8 January 2026 (6yr+B1 language / 4yr+EUR40k income / Finland degree / foreign degree+work / 4yr+C1 language)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Finland). MAJOR REFORM, effective 8 January 2026 (already in force as of this build): replaced a flat 4-years-of-A-permit rule with 5 alternative qualification paths, modeled here as 5 OR-groups since satisfying any one path qualifies. Path 3 (degree completed in Finland) is thin -- the specific residence/work-history minimums for this path specifically were not confirmed at tier-1 precision, only that it exists as a qualifying path; flagged as a gap. citizenship_after_months (0) on the outcome reflects that permanent residence itself is not a prerequisite for naturalisation eligibility timing in this dataset's model (naturalisation counts from continuous residence generally, not specifically from P-permit grant) -- see fi_naturalisation.json.
